label: end-of-input trigger (<DEL> or v/w/l/n/s/i/c/u) in sequences that start with j/r/m/p/k/b/y/0
explanation: Two-factor unit, active almost only during input (55% of mass) and at the <DEL> step (42%). It is nearly silent in the copy phase (3%) and never fires at t=0. Factor 1, the trigger: the current input is <DEL>, or the first occurrence of one of the letters v, w (strongest, 4x lift), l, n, s, or more weakly i, c, u. Factor 2, the context: the sequence starts with j/r/m/p/k/b/y/0, i.e. first_tok or the second original token is in that set (first_tok lift about 2x). When both of the first two tokens are in the set, <DEL> fires with about 80% precision. The context set looks like a slowly decaying memory of the opening tokens, so the unit is graded rather than crisp. Its rate rises at later original positions and with longer L. The largest activations are v or w near the end of the input, followed by <DEL>, in sequences starting with m/p/r/j. On its own, <DEL> fires on only 26% of sequences, and trigger letters fire on about 11-20% of their occurrences. The predicate gets dev F1 about 0.52 and mass recall about 0.74. The remaining misses come from weaker contexts (set tokens later in the prefix) that a two-token rule does not capture.
